page: Amazon Web Services x1.16xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine executed on the Xen hypervisor. It is powered by Intel Xeon E7-8880 v3 processors clocked at 2.3 GHz, delivering 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 32 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. The configuration includes 45 MB of shared L3 cache and supports standard x86 extensions, including AVX and AES-NI cryptographic acceleration. Hardware resources are bundled with 976 GB of system RAM, equating to 15.25 GB per vCPU, alongside 1,920 GB of integrated local SSD storage and a baseline network throughput of 10 Gbps. The instance does not include a GPU.

Benchmark data illustrates performance characteristics dictated by the Intel Haswell microarchitecture. Single-core processing metrics, including Geekbench and stress-ng single-thread runs, fall into the bottom tier compared to modern cloud processors. However, the high core count compensates during parallelized workloads, delivering median-tier multi-core results in PassMark (32,202.28) and stress-ng multi-core tests (30,370.67). Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate 133.54 GB/s read throughput and 65.16 GB/s write throughput on uncached large-block transfers. Operational benchmarks show strong memory-oriented execution, recording 8.34 million operations per second in Redis SET testing alongside steady Clang compilation throughput.

From an architectural standpoint, the x1.16xlarge prioritizes extreme memory capacity over per-core compute velocity. While modern instance families deliver higher instruction throughput for compute-bound tasks, this platform maximizes memory density without requiring distributed cluster partitioning. The integrated 1,920 GB local SSD storage provides fast scratch space for swap files or temporary index persistence. Consequently, the x1.16xlarge is appropriate for large-scale in-memory databases, memory-resident caching layers, big data analytics engines, and heavy relational database workloads that require extensive RAM allocations.
description: Amazon Web Services x1.16xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance configured with 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores powered by Intel Xeon E7-8880 v3 processors operating at 2.3 GHz. The instance delivers a massive 976 GB of system memory, providing approximately 15.25 GB of RAM per vCPU, alongside 1,920 GB of integrated local SSD storage and a 10 Gbps baseline network capability. Benchmark evaluations indicate modest single-thread CPU performance, with Geekbench single-core scoring in the lower tier, yet its 32 physical cores sustain average multi-core throughput in PassMark and stress-ng evaluations. Data-intensive benchmarks show solid throughput, achieving 8.34 million Redis SET operations per second and steady database processing metrics. The older Intel architecture trades per-core execution efficiency for vast memory capacity and dedicated core allocation. As a result, the x1.16xlarge is engineered primarily for high-density in-memory databases, large Redis or Memcached clusters, enterprise analytics, and extensive relational database caching layers.
